name: MK-677 for appetite/sleep

lead: MK-677 (ibutamoren) is an experimental oral drug that acts on the ghrelin receptor and raises growth hormone and IGF-1. Because ghrelin is the hunger hormone, and the drug increased REM and slow-wave sleep in a small human study, some users take it for stronger appetite and better sleep to support eating enough and recovering from training.

The chain to appearance is: more appetite and more sleep, then more eating and recovery, then more lean mass. Randomised trials in older adults found increased fat-free mass; users report hunger and sleep effects.

paras: People who use it describe it as an oral compound taken by mouth, often in the evening, and discuss appetite and sleep changes as the main early effects. This article does not give dosing or sourcing; the compound is an investigational drug, not an approved medicine.

Because the drug raises GH and IGF-1 and stimulates ghrelin signalling, researchers have measured effects on appetite, body composition and glucose handling. Case reports describe hepatotoxicity (2025) and reversible gynecomastia and hypogonadism with a performance supplement. It is an Investigational New Drug in the US and banned in most sports.

chain: Ghrelin-receptor agonism raises appetite and GH
More recovery and lean mass over time
angle.text: Users take MK-677 for the appetite and sleep effects as inputs to training, with gains in lean mass reported in older-adult trials.

lead: MK-677, also called ibutamoren, is an orally active, non-peptide agonist of the ghrelin receptor that raises growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) [1][2]. Merck developed it in the 1990s as a research drug; it has never been approved as a medicine and is described by Wikipedia and by the US Department of Defense supplement-safety programme as an investigational or research-only compound [3][4].

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums it is discussed mainly for two effects: stronger hunger and deeper sleep. Ghrelin is the stomach hormone that signals hunger, and a drug that mimics it can make eating larger amounts easier; a 1997 controlled study reported more deep and REM sleep in young and older volunteers [5]. Users describe the chain as more appetite and better sleep, then more food and recovery, then more lean mass over months, which shows up as a fuller physique. In a two-year randomised trial of healthy adults aged 60 to 81, daily MK-677 raised fat-free mass by roughly a kilogram over a year while the placebo group lost some [6].

The same trials documented the other side of the profile: transient swelling, higher fasting glucose and lower insulin sensitivity, and rising cortisol [6]. In 2025 the US Food and Drug Administration warned about a children's growth supplement that contained undeclared ibutamoren and listed appetite, water retention, fatigue, muscle pain and glucose changes among its possible effects [7]. Teenage users also discuss it for height, a use that no published trial in healthy adolescents has examined [8][9].

paras: MK-677 is a small, non-peptide molecule that binds the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, the receptor for the natural hormone ghrelin, and therefore signals the pituitary to release growth hormone in pulses [2][10]. Because it works by mouth, researchers studied it as an alternative to injected GH for frailty, GH deficiency and catabolic states [1][11]. Wikipedia lists it as raising cortisol as well as GH and IGF-1 [3].

Forum users often group it with peptides such as CJC-1295 and with injectable GH, although it is a small molecule rather than a peptide; one T Nation poster described it as a research chemical much cheaper than the peptide alternatives [12]. This article describes what has been reported and does not cover doses or where products are sold.

MK-677 emerged from Merck's work on orally active growth hormone secretagogues; a 1998 review in Annals of Medicine surveyed this class of oral compounds and their clinical prospects [1]. A 1996 study in healthy elderly subjects showed that once-daily oral dosing stimulated the GH-IGF-I axis [11], and a 1997 study found it did the same in selected GH-deficient adults [13].

Over 1997 to 1999, published trials examined sleep [5], two-month treatment in obese volunteers [14], calorie-restricted volunteers [15] and bone turnover markers in elderly adults [16]. In 2005 and 2009 pharmacology papers characterised how non-peptide and peptide secretagogues bind the ghrelin receptor [2][10]. A 2008 Annals of Internal Medicine trial in healthy older adults and a 2008 Alzheimer disease trial were later large publications [6][17]. The compound later came back under the name LUM-201 in a Phase 3 study in children with GH deficiency that began in 2026 [18].

Appetite is the effect most often mentioned by users. In the 2008 randomised trial, appetite increased early and subsided within a few months, while body weight rose 2.7 kg with MK-677 versus 0.8 kg with placebo over the year; the gain in fat-free mass was about 1.1 kg versus a 0.5 kg loss in controls, with no significant change in total fat or visceral fat, and limb fat rose more on the drug [6]. Strength and function were not improved in that study, which the authors said was underpowered for those endpoints [6].

A two-month trial in obese volunteers reported higher GH secretion, fat-free mass and energy expenditure [14], and a trial in dieting volunteers found the drug reversed diet-induced protein catabolism [15]. A 1999 analysis of the obesity trial noted that serum leptin did not track changes in body fat in the way expected, an observation about the interplay between GH and fat tissue [19]. A 2022 single-subject case report followed a user of MK-677 together with the SARM LGD-4033 and measured body composition, circulating biomarkers and muscle androgen-receptor content [20].

Users on T Nation describe taking it for appetite during bulking phases and, in one case, stopping and restarting because eating got out of control [21][22]. Another poster compared its results with pricier peptides and said they did not produce better results [12].

In a 1997 double-blind crossover study, eight young adults took MK-677 for seven days and six older adults for fourteen days; the researchers reported about 50 percent more stage IV (deep) sleep and over 20 percent more REM sleep in the young group at the higher dose, and nearly 50 percent more REM sleep in the older group [5]. Wikipedia summarises this work in the same terms [3]. The study was small, and no large trial has measured sleep as a primary outcome in people taking it for training.

Users on T Nation say joints felt better and recovery improved while taking it, while one poster added that this might be coincidence [23][24]. No trial has tested joint comfort in lifters; the older-adult trials measured IGF-1, body composition and function, and a Phase 2 fibromyalgia trial and a post-hip-fracture sarcopenia trial were also registered [25][26].

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities
paras: On T Nation, the MK-677/Ibutamoren thread from 2015 is a long-running place where users log daily morning use, weight changes and bloating [27]. The theme there and on looksmax.org is using it as an oral, inexpensive alternative to GH injections: one looksmax.org poster weighed pills against injectable HGH and others replied that both cause bloating [28].

Looksmax.org threads also discuss it for height in teens, for bone growth and for facial change, with titles such as a claimed safe and effective way to increase height, and a post reporting a measured wider face [9][29]. A teenage poster asked whether to buy it or HGH; another reply in the thread urged him to research it himself [8]. A T Nation thread asks whether GH can change the face at low or normal doses, with a user reporting he stayed in the low 100s on IGF-1 with MK-677 and thought HGH was his only route [30]. Others post about using it after a cut to gain without fat, or after a cycle of androgens, a pairing the FDA notice says may interact with SARMs [7][31].

The Department of Defense supplement program says products are sold with labels such as Supplement Facts, Research Facts or For Research Use Only, often combined with SARMs or labelled as SARMs [4]. A 2026 article in the American Journal of Sports Medicine discusses peptide supplements within sports medicine more broadly [32].

The 2008 trial reported transient mild leg swelling and muscle pain, a fasting glucose rise of about 0.3 mmol/L, lower insulin sensitivity, higher cortisol and bone-remodelling changes, and no serious adverse effects over twelve months [6]. The FDA's 2025 notice lists increased appetite, water retention, fatigue, muscle pain, glucose and insulin-sensitivity changes and, in certain people, possible risk of congestive heart failure, and says long-term effects are unknown [7]. The OPSS page says a clinical trial was stopped early over heart-failure rates and lists anxiety, diarrhoea, numbness and nausea among reported effects [4].

Two case reports describe organ-level effects: a man in his early thirties developed raised liver enzymes after two months of a supplement and recovered after stopping it, and the authors called reports of hepatotoxicity scarce [33]; a 2024 report described reversible gynecomastia and hypogonadism after a commercial performance supplement [34].

Ibutamoren is not approved for marketing in the United States, is not on the DEA's controlled-substance schedules and is on the WADA Prohibited List and the Department of Defense's prohibited-ingredient list [3][4]. The FDA has issued warning letters to sellers listing it among SARMs-labelled products, and its September 2025 notice describes lab testing that found undeclared ibutamoren in a children's growth supplement [7][4].

Randomised and controlled studies have examined MK-677 for GH/IGF-1 stimulation in healthy elderly subjects [11] and in GH-deficient adults [13], body composition in older adults [6], obese volunteers [14], diet-induced catabolism [15], sleep [5], bone turnover [16] and Alzheimer disease progression, where no clinical effect was found in a 512-participant Phase 2 trial [17][35]. Registered trials include one in 72 older adults on body composition and function [36], a fibromyalgia trial of 64 [25], a post-hip-fracture trial of 83 that was terminated [26], and a 12-person Phase 2 trial in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease completed in 2022 [37]. A Phase 3 trial of LUM-201 in children with growth hormone deficiency began in 2026 [18]. No trial has tested it in healthy young people for appearance.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org and T Nation, MK-677 is discussed as an oral, inexpensive way to raise GH and IGF-1 for appetite, sleep, recovery and, among teenagers, height and bone growth [27][28][9].
